analyzed_vuln.description: DnsLayer::parseResources() trusts the DNS header resource counts and constructs a DnsResource at offsetInPacket, then calls newResource->getSize() before validating that the resource's variable-length name and 10-byte fixed RR header are fully contained in m_Data. On a truncated resource, getSize() calls DnsResource::getDataLength(), which performs a 2-byte read of RDLENGTH past the packet buffer. The later `offsetInPacket > m_DataLen` check is too late because the out-of-bounds read has already occurred. Parsing must validate the current offset, decoded-name extent, fixed header/RDLENGTH field, and declared RDATA length against the remaining DNS bytes before computing/using the complete resource size.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A captured packet must be parsed through the FuzzTarget PCAP reader into IPv4/UDP DNS (source or destination DNS port, with at least a DNS header). The DNS count fields must advertise at least one non-query answer/authority/additional resource whose record begins near the end of the captured DNS payload or whose encoded name consumes the remaining bytes, leaving fewer than the required 10 fixed RR-header bytes (in this PoV, fewer than 2 bytes remain at the computed RDLENGTH position). The harness passes the captured RawPacket to Packet parsing; UdpLayer creates DnsLayer, parseResources follows the attacker-controlled counts/record bytes, and getSize/getDataLength reads the truncated RDLENGTH field out of bounds.

args: Analyze the root cause and safest minimal patch for the out-of-bounds read in DnsLayer::parseResources() in PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsLayer.cpp. Specifically explain how encoded DNS name length is represented by DnsResource/DnsQuery, whether getNameLength() itself is bounds-safe, and how to validate the name, the 10-byte fixed resource-record header, RDLENGTH, and RDATA before calling DnsResource::getSize(). Identify existing helper APIs or analogous validation elsewhere in this codebase.

The sanitizer reports a 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow in PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsResource.cpp DnsResource::getDataLength(), called by inline getSize() from PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsLayer.cpp parseResources(). The attacker controls DNS answer/authority/additional counts and supplies a truncated record near packet end. Current logic reportedly constructs a DnsResource at offsetInPacket and calls getSize() before checking offsetInPacket > m_DataLen. I have not edited anything yet. The desired patch must be confined to C/C++ under PcapPlusPlus, preserve valid DNS parsing, and reject/stop parsing malformed truncated resources before any unsafe access.
